_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4, the final reading). `pairs` is the approved plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides (IC4-R1).

pairs.line1: Give me a task and a few turns, Sire. I'll waste neither men nor days.
pairs.line2: Give me a task, Sire. What is put in my hands, I hold.

pairs.line1: Boldly, Sire? Straight at them with the columns.
pairs.line2: Boldly it is. Now I won't have to hold myself back.

pairs.line1: I held the squadrons back, Sire. Something changed out there.
pairs.line2: It changed, so I stayed on my own ground. Nobody shifts me off it.

pairs.line1: We got the worst of it, Sire. I'll look harder before the next assault.
pairs.line2: After that, Sire, I'm going very carefully indeed.

pairs.line1: I've made a small change, Sire. Nothing risky, I assure you.
pairs.line2: I've changed it, Sire. I'll stay on what is mine, but not like that.

pairs.line1: I see dust on the roads and none of it worth following.
pairs.line2: Nothing moving in front of me. The pickets are out.

pairs.line1: Moving up, Sire. Every wagon is closed up and every man accounted for.
pairs.line2: We marched hard today, Sire. I'd have gone faster if the men could.

pairs.line1: The corps is moving up, Sire, at a comfortable pace.
pairs.line2: On the road, Sire. We'll be up with them soon.

pairs.line1: Not three nights of the same, Sire, not for my columns. I've changed it.
pairs.line2: I'll not do the same thing a third night, Sire. A fixed habit gets men killed.

pairs.line1: Leave it with me, Sire. Once I have it in hand, I keep it.
pairs.line2: I'll see to it, Sire, and quickly. I can't bear sitting still.

pairs.line1: Done! Tell the others how it's managed.
pairs.line2: Finished. Send me to the next one who needs it.

pairs.line1: It is done, Sire, and without any fuss. I hope that counts.
pairs.line2: Was that not handsomely ridden, Sire?

rows.line: Every man was in place, so I sent them in, Sire.
I led the columns in myself, Sire. That's all.
I attacked, as it happens, Sire. I hope you understand it could not be helped.
They came too near my ground, so I hit them.
We rode at them. I'll not pretend I didn't enjoy it.
We went in at first light, Sire. I led from the front.
Half the country is behind my saddle already, Sire.
Moving up, Sire. Every wagon is closed up and every man accounted for.
On the road, Sire. Nothing I own is left open behind me.
On the road at last. We'll arrive when we arrive.
We marched hard today, Sire. I'd have gone faster if the men could.
Marching toward the sound of it, Sire.
A task for a cavalryman, Sire! I'll ride it in style.
Right, Sire. If the guns speak, I'll be there.
Very well, Sire. I'll start once the men are rested.
I'll check the rolls and the stores first, Sire. Then I begin.
I'll see to it, Sire, and quickly. I can't bear sitting still.
Leave it with me, Sire. Once I have it in hand, I keep it.
Done! Tell the others how it's managed.
The task is done, Sire. Now give me something worth fighting.
Finished. Send me to the next one who needs it.
The task is complete, Sire. The corps is intact.
The task is finished. My corps is whole.
The task is finished, Sire. Not an inch of it given back.
The guns told me it had changed, so I held the columns.
I held back, Sire, and I hated it. It had turned into a trap.
No move today. Here I know what I have.
The chance closed before I could get a squadron across.
Things shifted, Sire, so I held. Every man is where he should be.
I waited for a clearer picture, Sire. One can hardly be blamed.
